# User guide

The user guide is organized by topic: each page covers one in full, to read through or to look up when you need it. The [tutorials](tutorials.qmd) are the place to start; the user guide pages go further.

## Introduction

- [What is Starsim?](user_guide/intro_starsim.qmd): what Starsim is for, and what it does
- [Starsim models](user_guide/intro_models.qmd): models and frameworks built with Starsim
- [Conceptual overview](user_guide/intro_concepts.qmd): sims, modules, states, transitions, and solvers in one page

## Building models

- [Writing models](user_guide/building_writing.qmd): states, transitions, and rates, and checking what was built
- [Diseases](user_guide/building_diseases.qmd): the built-in diseases and writing your own
- [Parameters](user_guide/building_parameters.qmd): values, bounds, priors, and parameters that vary by group
- [Time](user_guide/building_time.qmd): dates, durations, rates, time steps, and values that change over time
- [Stratification](user_guide/building_stratification.qmd): splitting states by age, sex, risk, and more
- [Outcomes](user_guide/building_outcomes.qmd): reported cases, deaths, and other quantities derived from a model
- [Results](user_guide/building_results.qmd): reading, summarizing, and exporting results
- [Plotting](user_guide/building_plotting.qmd): plotting sims, results, and many runs
- [Custom modules](user_guide/building_modules.qmd): writing modules as code

## Populations and data

- [People and agents](user_guide/populations_people.qmd): the population, as compartments or as agents
- [Demographics](user_guide/populations_demographics.qmd): births, deaths, migration, and pregnancy
- [Contact networks](user_guide/populations_networks.qmd): who meets whom, from mixing pools to sexual networks
- [Population data](user_guide/populations_data.qmd): contact matrices and built-in data by country
- [Geography](user_guide/populations_geography.qmd): places, and movement between them

## Interventions and analyzers

- [Products](user_guide/interventions_products.qmd): vaccines, treatments, and diagnostics
- [Interventions](user_guide/interventions_interventions.qmd): delivering products, and changing parameters during a run
- [Analyzers](user_guide/interventions_analyzers.qmd): collecting results of your own
- [Connectors](user_guide/interventions_connectors.qmd): linking modules, e.g. diseases that interact
- [Costs](user_guide/interventions_costs.qmd): the costs of interventions, and cost per outcome averted

## Running models

- [Running sims](user_guide/running_sim.qmd): making and running a sim, and its settings
- [Scenarios](user_guide/running_scenarios.qmd): comparing scenarios, repeated runs, and uncertainty
- [Solvers and backends](user_guide/running_solvers.qmd): ODEs, stochastic compartments, and agents, and how one is chosen
- [Branching and rescaling](user_guide/running_branching.qmd): large populations and small outbreaks
- [Profiling and debugging](user_guide/running_debugging.qmd): finding what is slow or wrong, and common pitfalls
- [Deployment](user_guide/running_deploy.qmd): running Starsim on clusters and in the cloud

## Calibration

- [Fitting a model](user_guide/calibration_fitting.qmd): fitting parameters to data
- [Fitting methods](user_guide/calibration_methods.qmd): each method, what it needs, its settings, and an example
- [Fit diagnostics](user_guide/calibration_diagnostics.qmd): checking a fit
- [Parameter identification](user_guide/calibration_identification.qmd): which parameters the data can pin down
- [Gradients](user_guide/calibration_gradients.qmd): derivatives of results with respect to parameters
- [Optimization](user_guide/calibration_optimization.qmd): allocating a budget to get the best outcome

## Model library

- [Modeling landscape](user_guide/library_landscape.qmd): disease-modeling tools, and where Starsim fits
- [Library: diseases](user_guide/library_diseases.qmd): HIV, cholera, Ebola, measles, and more, ready to use
- [Library: networks](user_guide/library_networks.qmd): household, spatial, and theoretical networks
- [Library: maternal-child health](user_guide/library_mnch.qmd): fetal health, maternal infections, and neonatal outcomes
- [Conversion: import/export](user_guide/conversion/index.qmd): bringing models in from other frameworks, and writing them out

## Mechanics

- [Array indexing](user_guide/mechanics_indexing.qmd): agents, UIDs, and arrays
- [Distributions](user_guide/mechanics_distributions.qmd): random draws for agents
- [Random numbers](user_guide/mechanics_random.qmd): common random numbers, and comparing runs exactly
- [Nonstandard usage](user_guide/mechanics_nonstandard.qmd): agent-based models that are not about disease

## Architecture

- [Overview](user_guide/architecture_index.qmd): how Starsim works inside
- [Model declaration](user_guide/architecture_declaration.qmd): how a model is held as data
- [Model execution](user_guide/architecture_execution.qmd): how a model becomes a run
- [Solvers and backends](user_guide/architecture_solvers.qmd): the engines, and the kernels behind them
- [Transmission](user_guide/architecture_transmission.qmd): routes, effects, and results
- [Randomness](user_guide/architecture_randomness.qmd): random numbers, and fitting
- [Modules](user_guide/architecture_modules.qmd): what a module is, and how modules work together

::: {.callout-tip}
## Running the user guide locally

Each page can be downloaded as a Jupyter notebook: look for the download button at the top of the page. Or clone the Starsim repository, install Starsim (`pip install -e .`), go to `docs/user_guide`, and open the pages in Jupyter (`jupyter lab`).
:::
